parts: Sorry for yet another question, I am getting ready to present my model internally and I have a question on the model presented in the GWAS-by-subtraction paper as I have seen similar values in my own model. I am just wondering why the path loading (lambda Cog-CP) is 0.4465 and not closer to 1.0. All the best, Joan

messages.author: 0b5254eeb9973d7a
messages.subject: Re: GWAS-by-subtraction
parts:
The standardized loading of Cog Performance on Cog will be 1.0 as the residual variance of Cog Performance is constrained to 0. Since the Cog factor is scaled to have a variance of 1.0 (such that it is on a Z scale), the unstandardized loading of the Cog Performance variable on the Cog factor is a scaling constant. Squaring the unstandardized loading will give the SNP heritability.

I have a follow on question on sample size. I have followed the procedure of Perline Demange in her GitHub page to calculate sample size using the Cholesky model and just wanted to check where I obtain the value for path loadings . In figure 1 of the pre-print I can see where the value for cog is obtained but not noncog which I read as 0.2432. Am I misinterpreting from where this value is taken and once again thank you for your patience. 

All the best, Joan


cog$Neff <- ((cog$Z/(cog$est*sqrt(0.1993)))^2)/(2*cog$MAF*(1-cog$MAF)) #0.446483*0.446483=0.1993

noncog$Neff <- ((noncog$Z/(noncog$est*sqrt(0.0658)))^2)/(2*noncog$MAF*(1-noncog$MAF)) #0.256533*0.256533=0.0658
